title: Few-Shot Fine-Grained Entity Typing with Automatic Label Interpretation and Instance Generation

problem.claim: Few-shot fine-grained entity typing must classify entity mentions using only a few annotated mentions with contexts for each entity type.

gap.claim: Existing prompt-based approaches do not adequately account for target-corpus and label-hierarchy information in verbalizer construction and underuse the generation capability of pretrained language models.

contributions.claim: An automatic entity type label interpretation module relates type labels to vocabulary using few-shot instances and label hierarchy information.
A type-based contextualized instance generator creates new instances from given instances to enlarge the training set.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the proposed few-shot fine-grained entity typing framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On three benchmark datasets, the model reportedly outperforms existing methods by significant margins.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work studies few-shot fine-grained entity typing.
Prompt-based tuning reformulates entity type classification as a fill-in-the-blank task and can exploit pretrained language models.
Existing approaches have limitations in verbalizer construction and in exploiting language-model generation capabilities.
The proposed framework combines automatic label interpretation with type-based contextualized instance generation.
The authors report significant-margin improvements on three benchmark datasets.
